ja: 判断・決定を行うために用いる複数の基準
人・製品・提案などを評価または比較するための複数の尺度
選考・承認・資格取得などで満たすべき複数の条件
法律上の判断・権利取得・責任認定などに適用される複数の要件
研究・試験などで対象を含めたり除外したりするための基準
en: multiple standards used to make a judgment or decision
multiple measures used to evaluate or compare people, products, or proposals
multiple conditions that must be met for selection, approval, or qualification
multiple requirements applied to legal judgments, entitlement, or liability
standards used to include or exclude subjects in research or testing

nuance.ja: criteria は、判断のよりどころとなる複数の原則・条件・尺度を表す。単なる希望事項とは限らず、満たすか否かを評価できる一定の標準を含意する。selection criteria は候補者を選ぶための判断基準、eligibility criteria は資格の有無を決める条件である。requirements が必ず満たさなければならない義務的条件を指しやすいのに対し、criteria には、複数の候補を比較するための評価尺度も含まれる。criterion は単数、criteria は複数という区別が正式な文章では重要である。data と同様、英語内部で複数形が単数的に再解釈される傾向もあるが、特許・法律文書では伝統的な数の一致を維持するのが望ましい。
nuance.en: Criteria denotes multiple principles, conditions, or measures serving as a basis for judgment. The word normally implies standards against which something can be assessed, not merely desirable preferences. Selection criteria are used to compare and choose candidates, while eligibility criteria determine whether a person or entity qualifies. Requirements more strongly suggests mandatory conditions that must all be fulfilled, whereas criteria may also include evaluative measures used to rank alternatives. The distinction between singular criterion and plural criteria remains important in formal prose. Like data, criteria is increasingly reanalyzed as singular in some varieties, but traditional number agreement is advisable in patent, legal, academic, and other edited writing.

ja: criteria：判断・評価・選定に用いられる複数の基準。単数形は criterion。
criterion：判断の基準となる一つの原則・条件・尺度。
standards：品質・行為・性能などに期待または要求される水準。業界規格を指すことも多い。
requirements：承認・資格・契約履行などのために満たさなければならない必須条件。
conditions：ある結果や合意が成立するための条件。交渉上付された条件も含む。
qualifications：職務・資格などに必要な能力・経験・証明。
benchmarks：成果・品質・進捗を比較測定するための基準点。
factors：判断に影響を与える要素。必ずしも評価基準として明文化されていない。
en: criteria are multiple standards used for judgment, evaluation, or selection; the singular is criterion.
a criterion is one principle, condition, or measure serving as a basis for judgment.
standards are expected or required levels of quality, conduct, or performance and may also be formal industry specifications.
requirements are mandatory conditions that must be met for approval, qualification, or compliance.
conditions are circumstances or terms necessary for an outcome or agreement to take effect.
qualifications are the abilities, experience, or credentials needed for a role or status.
benchmarks are reference points used to measure and compare quality, achievement, or progress.
factors are elements influencing a decision and need not be formally defined as assessment standards.

etymology.ja: criteria は criterion の複数形で、ラテン語化されたギリシャ語 kritērion「判断する手段・基準」に由来する。これは kritēs「裁判官」と同じく、ギリシャ語 krinein「分ける、選ぶ、判断する」に基づく。この語根は crisis「重大な判断局面」、critic「批評家」、critical「批判的な・重大な」、discriminate「区別する」などにも歴史的につながる。ギリシャ語の中性名詞では単数形 -on に対して複数形 -a が用いられたため、英語でも criterion / criteria の組が継承された。
etymology.en: Criteria is the plural of criterion, which comes from Latinized Greek kriterion, meaning a means or standard of judgment. It is based on Greek krinein, meaning to separate, choose, or judge, and is related to krites, a judge. The same historical root appears in words such as crisis, critic, critical, and discriminate. Greek neuter nouns of this type formed the singular in -on and the plural in -a, and English inherited the pair criterion and criteria.

en: a single standard used as a basis for judgment or decision
one measure used to evaluate or compare a person, product, or proposal
one condition to be met for selection, approval, or qualification
one requirement used to determine a legal issue or entitlement
an indicator used to assess the validity of a theory, classification, or research result

nuance.ja: criterion は、複数の判断基準のうちの一つ、または判断を左右する単一の原則を指す。Price is an important criterion. といえば、価格が評価要素の一つであることを示す。The sole criterion is price. なら、価格だけが判断基準である。standard が達成すべき品質水準や一般的規範を表しやすいのに対し、criterion は、具体的な判断・分類・選択を行う際に適用する物差しに焦点を置く。法律・特許実務では、複数の要件のうち一つだけを指す場合に criterion を用いることで、criteria との数の区別を明確にできる。ただし、法令が充足を必須としている場合には requirement や condition のほうが強制性を正確に表すこともある。
nuance.en: Criterion refers to one of several possible standards or to a single principle controlling a judgment. Price is an important criterion identifies price as one evaluative factor, whereas The sole criterion is price states that no other standard applies. Standard often denotes an expected level of quality or a general norm, while criterion focuses on the measure used to make a particular judgment, classification, or selection. In legal and patent practice, criterion is useful when referring to only one element of a multi-part test and preserves the number distinction from criteria. If a rule makes compliance compulsory, however, requirement or condition may sometimes express that mandatory character more precisely.

ja: criterion：判断・評価・選定に用いる一つの基準。複数形は criteria。
criteria：複数の判断基準。正式な英語では複数動詞を取る。

en: a criterion is one standard used for judgment, evaluation, or selection; its plural is criteria.

a factor influences a decision but need not have been formally established as a standard.

etymology.ja: criterion はラテン語化されたギリシャ語 kritērion「判断する手段・基準」に由来する。これはギリシャ語 krinein「分ける、選ぶ、判断する」と、道具・手段を示す接尾要素 -tērion から成る。同じ語根は critic「批評家」、critical「批判的な・重大な」、crisis「重大な判断局面」などにも見られる。ギリシャ語の中性名詞では単数形 -on に対して複数形 -a が使われたため、英語にも criterion / criteria という単複の組が継承された。
etymology.en: Criterion comes from Latinized Greek kriterion, meaning a means or standard of judgment. It was formed from krinein, meaning to separate, choose, or judge, together with an element denoting an instrument or means. The same historical root appears in critic, critical, and crisis. Greek neuter nouns of this type used the singular ending -on and the plural ending -a, and English inherited the pair criterion and criteria.

usage.function: A conventional formal greeting used when two people are introduced for the first time.
usage.not_information_question: It does not normally request information about health, mood, or current circumstances.
usage.traditional_response: The traditional response is the identical formula How do you do?
usage.modern_response: Pleased to meet you, Very pleased to meet you, or It's a pleasure to meet you may also be used in modern interaction.
usage.frequency: Normally used only at the first introduction, not as a routine greeting between people who already know one another.
usage.register: Very formal and now somewhat old-fashioned, particularly associated with traditional British etiquette.
usage.punctuation: It is conventionally written as a question, although pragmatically it functions as a greeting rather than a genuine inquiry.
usage.intonation: Formal greeting intonation may be relatively level or falling, unlike a strongly information-seeking question.

ja: 初対面の相手に対して用いる、非常に改まった挨拶
正式な紹介を受けた際に、相手への礼儀と敬意を示す定型表現
伝統的には、同じ表現を返答として交わす挨拶
en: a highly formal greeting addressed to someone one is meeting for the first time
a conventional formula showing politeness and respect after a formal introduction
a greeting traditionally answered by repeating the same expression

nuance.ja: How do you do? は疑問文の形をしているが、How are you? のように体調や近況を尋ねるものではない。したがって、伝統的には I'm fine, thank you. ではなく、相手も How do you do? と返す。これは意味内容を交換するというより、正式な関係の開始を相互に確認する儀礼的な挨拶である。現在の日常会話ではかなり古風に響き、Nice to meet you. や Pleased to meet you. のほうが一般的である。ただし、格式のある式典、外交的・社交的な紹介、時代設定の古い作品などでは今も現れ得る。意図的に使えば上品・伝統的に聞こえるが、くだけた場面では堅苦しさや芝居がかった印象を与えることがある。
nuance.en: Although How do you do? has interrogative form, it does not seek information about health or current circumstances in the way How are you? does. Its traditional answer is therefore not I'm fine, thank you, but another How do you do? The exchange is ritual rather than informational and mutually recognizes the beginning of a formal acquaintance. In contemporary everyday interaction it sounds distinctly old-fashioned, and Nice to meet you or Pleased to meet you is much more common. It may still occur in ceremonial, diplomatic, or traditionally formal introductions and in works with a historical setting. Used deliberately, it can sound refined and traditional; in a casual setting, it may sound stiff or theatrical.

ja: How do you do?：正式な初対面で使う儀礼的挨拶。伝統的には同じ言葉で返す。
How are you?：相手の体調・気分・近況を尋ねる挨拶。初対面に限定されない。
Nice to meet you.：初対面で使う現代の標準的な挨拶。親しみやすく地域差が少ない。
Pleased to meet you.：初対面の喜びを示す、Nice to meet you より少し改まった表現。
It’s a pleasure to meet you.：初対面の相手への敬意を示す、丁寧で職業的な挨拶。
Hello.：初対面か既知かを問わず使える一般的な挨拶。
How have you been?：以前から知る相手に、しばらく会わなかった間の近況を尋ねる。
What do you do?：職業を尋ねる質問。How do you do? とは意味がまったく異なる。
en: How do you do? is a ritual formal greeting used at a first introduction and traditionally answered with the same words.
How are you? asks about health, mood, or general circumstances and is not limited to first meetings.
Nice to meet you is the standard modern first-meeting greeting and sounds friendly and regionally neutral.
Pleased to meet you expresses pleasure at the introduction and is slightly more formal than Nice to meet you.
It's a pleasure to meet you is a polite professional greeting conveying respect.
Hello is a general greeting usable with both new acquaintances and people already known.
How have you been? asks an existing acquaintance about the period since the last meeting.
What do you do? asks about occupation and is entirely different in meaning from How do you do?

etymology.ja: この表現の do は、現代の「行う」だけでなく、かつて一般的だった「暮らす、具合が～である、やっていく」という意味に関係する。How do you do? は歴史的には「どのようにお過ごしですか」「ご機嫌はいかがですか」に相当する実質的な質問だったが、繰り返し用いられるうちに意味が薄れ、初対面の儀礼的な定型句となった。do は古英語 dōn「行う、置く、～の状態にする」に由来する。現代では構成語から意味を計算するより、一まとまりの挨拶として理解される。
etymology.en: The do in this expression is connected with an older sense meaning fare, get along, or be in a particular condition, rather than only the modern sense perform an action. How do you do? historically functioned more literally as a question equivalent to How are you faring? Through repeated conventional use, its informational content weakened and it became a ritual greeting for first introductions. Do derives from Old English don, meaning to perform, put, or cause to be in a state. Modern speakers generally process the entire expression as one greeting rather than interpreting each word independently.

note.ja: 初対面の喜びを丁寧に伝える。現代でも自然で、How do you do? より堅苦しくない。
note.en: Politely expresses pleasure at a first meeting and remains natural in modern use without sounding as stiff.

note.ja: 現代の初対面で最も一般的な挨拶。正式・非正式の幅広い場面に適する。
note.en: The most common modern greeting at a first meeting, suitable for a wide range of formal and informal situations.

She greeted each guest with a handshake and a formal How do you do? — 彼女は一人一人の客に握手し、正式な「はじめまして」の挨拶をした。
In most modern business meetings, Nice to meet you sounds more natural than How do you do? — 現代のビジネス会議の大半では、How do you do? より Nice to meet you. のほうが自然に聞こえる。
How do you do? I understand that your firm handles patent prosecution in Germany. — はじめまして。貴所ではドイツの特許出願手続を取り扱っていると伺っております。
en: Lady Harrington, may I introduce Dr. Lewis? — How do you do? — How do you do?
How do you do, Mr. Brown? I have heard a great deal about your work.
She greeted each guest with a handshake and a formal How do you do?
In most modern business meetings, Nice to meet you sounds more natural than How do you do?
How do you do? I understand that your firm handles patent prosecution in Germany.

patterns: Not much. What’s up with you?

usage.greeting: Used as a casual greeting similar to How's it going? and may not require a detailed answer.
usage.problem: Used when someone appears troubled or behaves unusually, meaning What is the matter?
usage.situation: Used to ask what is happening or what the current situation is.
usage.with_construction: What's up with someone or something asks why that person or thing is behaving unusually or what explains the situation.
usage.response: Common greeting responses include Not much, Nothing much, I'm good, and The usual, often followed by And you?
usage.register: Very informal; suitable among friends and familiar colleagues but generally not for formal introductions or client correspondence.
usage.regional_note: Strongly associated with American English but now widely understood throughout the English-speaking world.
usage.spelling: The apostrophe is required in standard writing because what's contracts what is.

ja: 友人・知人への気軽な挨拶として、最近どうか尋ねる
今何をしているのか、どんな予定があるのか尋ねる
現在何が起きているのか、状況や最新情報を尋ねる
相手の様子が普段と違うとき、どうしたのか尋ねる
人・物・事態について、異常や問題の理由を尋ねる
en: used as a casual greeting asking how someone is or what is new
used to ask what someone is doing or planning
used to ask what is currently happening or what the latest situation is
used to ask what is wrong when someone appears upset or behaves unusually
used with with to ask what explains a strange person, thing, or situation

nuance.ja: What’s up? は文脈と口調によって、軽い挨拶にも、本当の状況確認にもなる。笑顔で Hey, what’s up? と言えば「やあ、調子はどう？」に近く、通常は長い説明を期待せず、Not much. や I’m good. で答えられる。一方、沈んだ表情の人に You seem worried. What’s up? と尋ねれば、「何かあったの？」「どうしたの？」という実質的な質問になる。What’s up with the printer? は、プリンターに何か異常があることを前提として、その原因を尋ねる。このため、単独の表現を機械的に一つの日本語へ訳すのではなく、挨拶・予定・異常のどれを尋ねているか判断する必要がある。
nuance.en: What's up? may be either a light greeting or a genuine request for information, depending on context and intonation. Said cheerfully as Hey, what's up?, it resembles How's it going? and normally does not invite a lengthy account; Not much or I'm good is sufficient. Said to someone who looks distressed, as in You seem worried. What's up?, it becomes a substantive question meaning What happened? or What's wrong? What's up with the printer? presupposes that something about the printer is unusual and asks for an explanation. The expression should therefore be interpreted according to whether the speaker is greeting someone, asking about plans, or investigating a problem.

ja: what’s up?：気軽な挨拶として近況を尋ねる、または何が起きたか・どうしたか尋ねる。
how are you?：健康・気分・近況を尋ねる標準的な挨拶。what’s up? より広い場面に適する。
how’s it going?：生活・仕事などがどのように進んでいるかを気軽に尋ねる。
what’s happening?：現在起きている出来事や状況を比較的直接的に尋ねる。
what’s wrong?：相手や物に問題があると考え、その問題が何かを尋ねる。
what’s the matter?：不調・動揺・問題の理由を尋ねる。what’s up? より問題の存在を強く想定する。
what are you up to?：今していること、または近頃取り組んでいることを尋ねる。
how do you do?：正式な初対面の儀礼的挨拶であり、what’s up? とは格式も用途も大きく異なる。
en: what's up? is a casual greeting or a question asking what is happening or what is wrong.
how are you? is a standard greeting asking about health or general condition and suits a broader range of contexts.
how's it going? casually asks how life, work, or a current situation is progressing.
what's happening? more directly asks about current events or activity.
what's wrong? assumes that a person or thing has a problem and asks what it is.
what's the matter? asks about the cause of distress or difficulty and more strongly presupposes a problem.
what are you up to? asks what someone is doing now or has been occupied with recently.
how do you do? is a ritual greeting for a formal first introduction and differs sharply in register and function.

etymology.ja: up は古英語 up・uppe「上へ、上に」に由来する。空間的な「上」の意味から、活動中・発生中・問題が表面化した状態などを表すようになった。What is up? は文字どおりには「何が持ち上がっているのか」だが、やがて「何が起きているのか」「何が問題なのか」を尋ねる表現となった。19世紀以前から関連する用法が見られ、20世紀のアメリカ英語で日常的な挨拶として特に定着した。のちに短縮発音を写した Whassup?、Wassup?、Sup? などの俗語的な形も生まれた。
etymology.en: Up derives from Old English up and uppe, meaning upward or in a higher position. From its spatial meaning developed senses associated with activity, occurrence, availability, and a problem coming to attention. What is up? thus moved from a literal spatial interpretation to asking what is happening or what is the matter. Related uses have a long history, and the expression became particularly established as an everyday greeting in American English during the twentieth century. Highly informal spellings such as Whassup?, Wassup?, and Sup? later arose to represent reduced pronunciation.

note.ja: 相手の生活・仕事・状況がどう進んでいるかを尋ねる、くだけた挨拶。
note.en: A casual greeting asking how life, work, or a current situation is progressing.

note.ja: 現在の出来事・活動・状況について尋ねる。挨拶として使われることもある。
note.en: Asks about current events, activity, or circumstances and may also function as a greeting.

note.ja: 問題が存在すると想定し、その内容を直接尋ねる。
note.en: Assumes that a problem exists and directly asks what it is.

note.ja: 前回会ってからの新しい出来事や近況を尋ねる気軽な挨拶。
note.en: A casual greeting asking about new developments since the previous interaction.

equivalents.de: Was ist los? / Was geht?
equivalents.it: Come va? / Che succede? / Che c’è?
equivalents.fr: Quoi de neuf ? / Qu’est-ce qui se passe ?
equivalents.es: ¿Qué tal? / ¿Qué pasa?

ja: What’s up? — 最近どう、どうしたの
Hey, what’s up? — やあ、調子はどう
What’s up with you? — 君はどうしたの
What’s up with that? — あれは一体どういうことなの
What’s up with the computer? — コンピューターはどうしたの
What’s been up lately? — 最近どうしていたの
Do you know what’s up? — 何が起きているか知っていますか
tell me what’s up — 事情を教えて
Not much. — 特に何もないよ
Nothing much. How about you? — 特に何も。あなたはどう
en: What’s up?
Hey, what’s up?
What’s up with you?
What’s up with that?
What’s up with the computer?
What’s been up lately?
Do you know what’s up?
tell me what’s up
Not much.
Nothing much. How about you?

ja: Hey, what’s up? — Not much. How about you? — 「やあ、最近どう？」「特に何も。そっちは？」
You’ve been unusually quiet today. What’s up? — 今日はいつになく静かですね。どうしたのですか。
What’s up with the printer? It keeps making a strange noise. — プリンターはどうしたのでしょう。変な音が鳴り続けています。
Could you fill me in on what’s up with the negotiations? — 交渉が今どうなっているのか、事情を教えてもらえますか。
The client has requested an urgent call. Do you know what’s up with the patent application? — 依頼人から緊急の電話会議を求められました。特許出願に何が起きているか知っていますか。
en: Hey, what’s up? — Not much. How about you?
You’ve been unusually quiet today. What’s up?
What’s up with the printer? It keeps making a strange noise.
Could you fill me in on what’s up with the negotiations?
The client has requested an urgent call. Do you know what’s up with the patent application?

patterns: I don’t envy you one bit.
I don’t envy you having to + verb.
I don’t envy you for having to + verb.
I don’t envy you the task of + gerund.
I wouldn’t envy anyone in your position.
I don’t envy whoever has to + verb.
No one envies someone having to + verb.

usage.pragmatic_meaning: Normally expresses sympathy for someone facing an unpleasant, difficult, or awkward situation.
usage.literal_structure: Envy is negated, but the conversational force is often equivalent to I am glad I am not in your position.
usage.following_action: The difficulty may be expressed with having to: I don't envy you having to tell them.
usage.for_construction: For having to is also possible and makes the reason for the sympathy explicit.
usage.task_construction: Especially in British English, I don't envy you the task of doing something may identify an unwelcome responsibility.
usage.intensification: One bit, at all, or certainly may strengthen the expression.
usage.register: Conversational and generally sympathetic, though tone can make it teasing, ironic, or smug.
usage.pronoun_variation: The object can change according to context: I don't envy him, her, them, or anyone in that position.

ja: 困難・不快な状況にいる相手へ同情を示す
自分なら相手の立場にはなりたくないと伝える
相手が引き受ける仕事・決断・責任が大変だと認める
これから経験することが容易ではないと、軽く警告する
文字どおり、相手の持つものや立場を羨ましく思わない
en: used to express sympathy for someone in a difficult or unpleasant situation
used to say that the speaker would not want to be in the other person's position
used to acknowledge that someone's task, decision, or responsibility will be difficult
used as a mild warning that an approaching experience will not be easy
literally, to say that one does not desire another person's possession or position

nuance.ja: I don’t envy you. は、通常、羨望が存在しないことを冷淡に述べるのではなく、相手の置かれた状況の厳しさを認める共感表現である。You have to tell the client that the application was refused? I don’t envy you. なら、「それを伝えるのはつらいでしょうね」という意味になる。Sorry to hear that. が起きた不幸への直接的な同情であるのに対し、I don’t envy you. は、相手がこれから行わなければならない困難な仕事や、対処すべき板挟みの状況に特に自然である。ただし、笑いながら言うと親しい間柄での軽いからかいとなり、優越感のある口調では「あなたでなくてよかった」という無神経な響きにもなり得る。
nuance.en: I don’t envy you normally does not make a cold factual statement about the absence of envy. It acknowledges how difficult or unpleasant the listener's situation is. In You have to tell the client that the application was refused? I don’t envy you, the speaker means that delivering the news will be difficult and expresses sympathy. Sorry to hear that responds directly to misfortune that has occurred, while I don’t envy you is especially natural when the listener must perform a difficult task or manage an awkward dilemma. Said with laughter, it may be affectionate teasing between friends; delivered with a superior tone, it may sound insensitive or smugly imply that the speaker is pleased not to be involved.

ja: I don’t envy you.：大変な状況にいる相手へ、「私ならその立場にはなりたくない」と同情を示す。
I envy you.：相手の持つ物・経験・立場を自分も欲しいと羨む。
I’m sorry to hear that.：相手に起きた悪い出来事を聞き、直接的に同情を示す。
You have my sympathy.：相手の困難への同情を明示する、やや改まった表現。
I feel for you.：相手の苦しさが分かると、温かく感情的に共感する。
I wouldn’t want to be in your shoes.：相手の立場を想像し、自分ならその状況を避けたいと強く述べる。
Good luck with that.：困難な仕事について成功を祈る。口調によっては皮肉にもなる。
Better you than me.：自分でなく相手が引き受けてよかったと述べるため、より率直で無神経になり得る。
en: I don’t envy you expresses sympathy by saying that the speaker would not want to face the listener's difficult situation.
I envy you means that the speaker desires a possession, experience, or advantage enjoyed by the listener.
I’m sorry to hear that directly expresses sympathy upon hearing bad news.
You have my sympathy explicitly acknowledges another person's difficulty and is somewhat formal.
I feel for you expresses warm emotional empathy with another person's suffering.
I wouldn’t want to be in your shoes strongly imagines and rejects the prospect of occupying the listener's position.
Good luck with that wishes someone success with a difficult task but may sound ironic depending on tone.
Better you than me openly states relief that the other person, rather than the speaker, must face the situation and may sound insensitive.

etymology.ja: envy は古フランス語 envie を経て、ラテン語 invidia「羨望・悪意」に由来する。invidia は invidēre「羨む、敵意をもって見る」から生じ、in-「～に対して」と vidēre「見る」から成る。語源的には、他人の幸運を好ましくない目で見るという発想を持つ。I don’t envy you. は、この羨望を否定する文字どおりの文から、「その状況には望ましいところがない」「自分ならその立場になりたくない」という推意が生まれ、困難な立場にいる人への同情表現として定着した。
etymology.en: Envy entered English through Old French envie from Latin invidia, meaning envy, ill will, or hostility. Invidia derived from invidere, to envy or look at with hostility, formed from in-, toward or against, and videre, to see. The etymological image is that of looking unfavorably upon another person's good fortune. From the literal negative statement I do not desire your position arose the implication that the position contains nothing desirable and that the speaker would not wish to occupy it. The sentence consequently became a conventional expression of sympathy for someone facing difficulty.

synonyms.word: I wouldn’t want to be in your shoes

note.ja: 相手の立場を自分に置き換えて考え、その困難を強く認める比喩表現。
note.en: A figurative expression strongly acknowledging the difficulty by imagining oneself in the listener's position.

note.ja: 相手の苦痛・失望などに、感情的な共感を示す温かい表現。
note.en: A warm expression of emotional empathy with another person's pain or disappointment.

note.ja: 困難な状況にある相手へ同情を明示する、比較的改まった表現。
note.en: A relatively formal statement explicitly offering sympathy to someone in difficulty.

note.ja: 相手の仕事・経験・状況が大変そうだと、日常的に共感を示す。
note.en: An everyday response acknowledging that another person's task or experience sounds difficult.

equivalents.de: Ich beneide dich / Sie nicht. / Ich möchte nicht in deiner / Ihrer Haut stecken.
equivalents.it: Non ti / La invidio. / Non vorrei essere nei tuoi / Suoi panni.
equivalents.fr: Je ne vous / t’envie pas. / Je ne voudrais pas être à votre / ta place.
equivalents.es: No te / le envidio. / No me gustaría estar en tu / su lugar.

ja: I don’t envy you. — それは大変ですね
I don’t envy you one bit. — あなたの立場はまったく羨ましくありません
I certainly don’t envy you. — 本当に大変だと思います
I don’t envy you having to decide. — あなたが決断しなければならないのは大変ですね
I don’t envy you for having to tell them. — あなたが彼らに伝えなければならないのはつらいですね
I don’t envy you the task of explaining it. — それを説明する役目は大変でしょう
I wouldn’t envy anyone in that position. — その立場には誰であってもなりたくないでしょう
I don’t envy whoever has to deal with it. — それに対処する人は大変でしょう
I don’t envy him his responsibilities. — 彼の負っている責任は羨ましくない
I don’t envy your commute. — あなたの通勤は大変そうですね
en: I don’t envy you.
I don’t envy you one bit.
I certainly don’t envy you.
I don’t envy you having to decide.
I don’t envy you for having to tell them.
I don’t envy you the task of explaining it.
I wouldn’t envy anyone in that position.
I don’t envy whoever has to deal with it.
I don’t envy him his responsibilities.
I don’t envy your commute.

ja: You have to work all weekend? I don’t envy you. — 週末ずっと働かなければならないのですか。それは大変ですね。
I don’t envy you having to choose between those two options. — その二つの選択肢から選ばなければならないとは、大変ですね。
She has to dismiss half of the team, and I certainly don’t envy her. — 彼女はチームの半数を解雇しなければならず、本当に大変な立場だと思う。
I don’t envy you the task of explaining the additional costs to the client. — 追加費用を依頼人に説明する役目は大変でしょう。
You have to tell the inventor that the disclosure may have jeopardized patentability? I don’t envy you. — その開示によって特許性が危うくなった可能性を発明者へ伝えなければならないのですか。それはつらい役目です。
en: You have to work all weekend? I don’t envy you.
I don’t envy you having to choose between those two options.
She has to dismiss half of the team, and I certainly don’t envy her.
I don’t envy you the task of explaining the additional costs to the client.
You have to tell the inventor that the disclosure may have jeopardized patentability? I don’t envy you.

grammar.countability: usually uncountable; countable when referring to a particular cause or instance of envy
patterns: be the envy of + person / group

usage.person_object: Envy someone means to desire an advantage, possession, quality, or experience that the person has.
usage.reason: The reason may be introduced with for: I envy her for her confidence.
usage.double_object: The construction envy someone something is possible: I envy you your freedom.
usage.possessive_object: The desired quality or possession may be used directly: I envy his patience.
usage.noun: As an emotion, envy is normally uncountable: She felt envy, not normally an envy.
usage.be_the_envy_of: To be the envy of a group means to possess something that the other members would like to have.
usage.register: Neutral and usable in conversation, literature, academic discussion, and formal writing.
usage.spelling: Change y to i before -es and -ed: envies, envied; retain y before -ing: envying.

ja: 他人が持つ物・能力・地位・経験などを自分も欲しいと思う
他人の恵まれた状態を羨ましく感じる
他人の成功や優位に不満・反感を伴う羨望を感じる
他人の所有物や長所を望ましく思う感情
多くの人が羨む人物・物・状態
en: to wish that one had another person's possession, ability, position, or experience
to feel desire for an advantage enjoyed by someone else
to feel resentful desire in response to another person's success or superiority
the feeling of wanting something possessed or enjoyed by another person
a person, possession, or condition that others strongly wish they had

nuance.ja: envy は、自己と他者を比較し、相手が持っている望ましいものを自分も欲しいと感じる感情である。I envy your patience. は、相手の忍耐力を高く評価し、自分にもあればよいと思う比較的穏やかな羨望になり得る。一方、envy には、相手がその利点を失えばよいと願うような不満・敵意が伴う場合もある。心理学では、相手を見習おうとする benign envy と、相手を引き下ろそうとする malicious envy を区別することがある。日常英語では jealous が envy の意味でも広く使われるが、伝統的な区別では envy は他人の持つものを欲する二者関係、jealousy は第三者に愛情・地位などを奪われることへの警戒を含む三者関係に焦点を置く。
nuance.en: Envy arises from comparison with another person and desire for an advantage that the other person possesses. I envy your patience can be a mild, admiring statement meaning that the speaker wishes to possess the same quality. Envy may also include resentment or a wish that the other person lose the advantage. Psychological discussion sometimes distinguishes benign envy, which motivates self-improvement, from malicious envy, which motivates pulling the other person down. In everyday English, jealous is widely used in the sense of envious. Under the traditional distinction, however, envy is a two-party relation involving desire for what another has, whereas jealousy commonly involves fear that a third party will take away one's affection, status, or advantage.

ja: envy：他人が持つ望ましい物・能力・経験などを、自分も欲しいと感じる。
jealousy：人間関係や地位を第三者に奪われることへの不安・警戒。日常語では envy の意味にも使われる。
admiration：人の能力・人格・業績を高く評価すること。自分も欲しいという比較は必須ではない。
covet：他人の所有物などを、自分のものにしたいと強く欲する。否定的・宗教的な響きを持ち得る。
resentment：不当な扱い・侮辱・格差などに対して持続的な怒りや不満を感じること。
longing：手に入りにくい人・物・状態を強く切望する。比較対象としての他人は必要ない。
be envious of：人やその所有物を羨ましく思う。envy の形容詞構文。
be the envy of：他の人々から羨ましがられる存在である。羨望を感じる側ではない。
en: envy is the desire to possess an attractive object, ability, or experience enjoyed by someone else.
jealousy is traditionally anxiety about losing a relationship or position to a third party, though it commonly overlaps with envy in everyday speech.
admiration is high regard for another person's ability, character, or achievement and does not require self-comparison.
covet means to desire another person's possession strongly and may carry negative or religious connotations.
resentment is lasting anger or dissatisfaction caused by perceived unfairness, insult, or inequality.
longing is an intense desire for a person, object, or state that may be difficult to obtain and requires no comparison with another person.
be envious of is the adjectival construction corresponding to the verb envy.
be the envy of means to be admired and desired by others rather than to experience envy oneself.

etymology.ja: envy は古フランス語 envie「羨望・悪意」を経て、ラテン語 invidia に由来する。invidia は動詞 invidēre「羨む、悪意をもって見る」から生じ、in-「～に対して」と vidēre「見る」から成る。語源的には、他人の幸福や優位を好ましくない目で見るという発想を持つ。イタリア語 invidia、フランス語 envie、スペイン語 envidia は同じラテン語に由来する。ただし現代フランス語 envie は「欲求・～したい気持ち」という、必ずしも他人との比較を含まない広い意味でも頻用される。
etymology.en: Envy entered English through Old French envie, meaning envy or ill will, from Latin invidia. Invidia was derived from invidere, to envy or look at with hostility, formed from in-, toward or against, and videre, to see. Its etymological image is that of looking unfavorably at another person's happiness or advantage. Italian invidia, French envie, and Spanish envidia derive from the same Latin source. Modern French envie, however, also commonly means desire or inclination without necessarily involving comparison with another person.

note.ja: 日常語では envy と重なるが、伝統的には愛情・地位などを奪われる不安を表す。
note.en: Often overlaps with envy in everyday use but traditionally denotes fear of losing affection or status.

note.ja: 他人の所有物・富・地位などを自分のものにしたいという強い欲望。
note.en: A strong and often morally disapproved desire to possess another person's property, wealth, or position.

note.ja: 不公平だと感じる状況に対して抱く、持続的な怒り・苦々しさ。
note.en: Persistent anger or bitterness in response to a situation perceived as unfair.

note.ja: 人物・能力・成果を高く評価する肯定的な感情で、敵意や自己比較を必要としない。
note.en: Positive regard for a person, ability, or achievement without requiring hostility or self-comparison.

equivalents.de: Neid / beneiden

patterns: several days / weeks / months in advance

usage.standalone: In advance functions adverbially without an object: Please book in advance.
usage.of_construction: In advance of is followed by a noun and means before or in preparation for it.
usage.time_measurement: A duration may precede the phrase: three weeks in advance.
usage.intensifiers: Well in advance and far in advance emphasize a substantial amount of preparation time.
usage.payment: Pay in advance means to make payment before goods or services are delivered.
usage.article: No article is used in the fixed phrase: in advance, not in an advance.
usage.register: Neutral and common in everyday, business, legal, and formal contexts.
usage.email_formula: Thank you in advance anticipates compliance with a request and may sound efficient, appreciative, or presumptuous depending on context.

ja: 予定された出来事・期限・必要時点より前に
必要になることを見越して、あらかじめ
会議・発表・変更などに先立って

依頼への対応が行われる前に、先に感謝を示して
en: before a scheduled event, deadline, or point of need
beforehand, in anticipation of a future need
before and sometimes in preparation for a meeting, announcement, change, or other event
with payment made before goods or services are supplied
with thanks expressed before the requested action has been performed

nuance.ja: in advance は、単に時間的に先であるだけでなく、将来の出来事を予測して準備・予約・通知・支払いなどを済ませるという含みを持つことが多い。Please let us know in advance. は、相手が行動する前に知らせてほしいという意味であり、具体的な期間を示すなら at least two weeks in advance のように言う。in advance of the meeting は before the meeting よりやや形式的で、会議に備えて行われるという関係も示しやすい。Thank you in advance. は依頼メールで頻用されるが、まだ承諾されていない作業について先に礼を言うため、相手に断りにくさを感じさせることがある。より柔らかくするなら Thank you for considering my request. や I would appreciate your help. が使える。
nuance.en: In advance often conveys more than simple temporal priority. It commonly suggests anticipation and preparation for a future event through booking, notification, planning, or payment. Please let us know in advance asks for notice before the relevant action occurs; a specific interval can be given as at least two weeks in advance. In advance of the meeting is somewhat more formal than before the meeting and may more readily imply preparation for it. Thank you in advance is common in request emails, but because it expresses thanks before the other person has agreed to act, it can create pressure or sound presumptuous. Thank you for considering my request or I would appreciate your help may be softer alternatives.

ja: in advance：将来の出来事や必要を見越し、予定時点より前に準備・予約・通知などを行って。
beforehand：ある出来事の前に。in advance より会話的で、準備の含みは弱い場合がある。
ahead of time：予想・予定された時刻より早く。予定より早く完了したという意味にもなる。
in advance of：特定の出来事に先立って、またはそれに備えて。
before：二つの時点・出来事の時間的な前後関係を表す最も一般的な語。
prior to：～より前に、を表す形式的な前置詞句。
up front：費用などを最初に全額支払う、または情報を最初から率直に示す。
prepaid：代金があらかじめ支払われている状態を表す形容詞。
en: in advance means before the expected time, often with preparation for a future event or need.
beforehand means before an event and is more conversational, sometimes with less emphasis on preparation.
ahead of time means earlier than expected or scheduled and may describe early completion.
in advance of means before a specified event and often in preparation for it.
before is the most general word for temporal priority between events or times.
prior to is a formal prepositional phrase meaning before.
up front means paying a cost at the beginning or stating information openly from the outset.
prepaid is an adjective indicating that payment has already been made.

etymology.ja: advance は古フランス語 avancer「前へ進める」に由来する。これは後期ラテン語 abante「前方へ」にさかのぼり、ab「～から」と ante「前に」から成る。英語では物理的に前進する意味から、時間・発展・地位などで先へ進む意味が生じた。in advance は、時間的に出来事より前の位置にいるという比喩から、「前もって、あらかじめ」を意味するようになった。なお、フランス語 avant「前に」、イタリア語 avanti「前へ」、スペイン語 avanzar「前進する」も歴史的に関連する。
etymology.en: Advance entered English through Old French avancer, meaning to move forward. It ultimately relates to Late Latin abante, forward or from before, formed from ab, from, and ante, before. From physical forward movement, advance developed senses involving progress in time, position, and development. In advance arose from the metaphor of occupying a point ahead of an event in time and came to mean beforehand or in anticipation. French avant, Italian avanti, and Spanish avanzar belong to the same broader historical family.

note.ja: 出来事が起きる前に行うことを表す一般的な副詞。日常会話でも自然。
note.en: A general adverb meaning before an event, natural in everyday conversation.

note.ja: 予想される問題・行動を防ぐため、相手や事態に先んじて措置を取ることを表す。
note.en: Describes acting first in order to prevent or forestall an anticipated problem or action.

usage.thing: When applied to a task, explanation, process, or issue, straightforward means uncomplicated and easy to understand or deal with.
usage.person: When applied to a person, answer, or manner, it means direct, honest, and free from concealment.
usage.infinitive: Be straightforward to do means that the action can be performed without complicated reasoning or procedure.
usage.preposition_about: Be straightforward about something means to discuss that subject honestly and directly.
usage.preposition_with: Be straightforward with someone means to communicate openly with that person.
usage.spelling: The adjective is normally written as one word: straightforward.
usage.comparison: More straightforward and most straightforward are preferable to straightforwarder and straightforwardest.
usage.register: Neutral and suitable for conversation, business, academic, technical, and legal contexts.

ja: 構造・手順・内容などが単純で理解しやすい
実行・処理・解決の方法が明確で複雑ではない
判断や結論へ至る道筋が明白である
発言・説明などが遠回しでなく率直である
人が正直で隠し立てをせず、扱いやすい
en: simple in structure, procedure, or content and easy to understand
clear and uncomplicated to perform, handle, or solve
having an obvious line of reasoning toward a judgment or conclusion
direct and honest rather than indirect or evasive
open, sincere, and uncomplicated in dealing with other people

nuance.ja: straightforward の中心的なイメージは、目的地まで曲がりくねらず、まっすぐ前へ進めることである。a straightforward procedure は手順が明確で余計な複雑さがなく、a straightforward answer は質問に直接答え、曖昧化や回避をしない。easy は必要な能力や労力が少ないことを表すが、straightforward は方法や論理が明瞭であることを表すため、The work is time-consuming but straightforward.「時間はかかるが、作業自体は単純明快だ」のように両立する。人について使う場合は通常肯定的だが、率直すぎて配慮に欠けるという意味は必ずしも含まない。そうした否定的な率直さには blunt のほうが適する。
nuance.en: The central image of straightforward is a route leading directly forward without turns or complications. A straightforward procedure has clear steps and no unnecessary complexity, while a straightforward answer responds directly without evasion or obscurity. Easy describes something requiring little effort or ability, whereas straightforward describes a clear method or line of reasoning. The work is time-consuming but straightforward is therefore entirely coherent. When applied to a person, the word is normally complimentary and suggests honesty and ease of dealing. It does not inherently imply insensitivity or excessive directness; blunt is more appropriate for that negative quality.

ja: straightforward：手順・意味・論理が明瞭で複雑でない。または人・発言が率直である。
easy：必要な労力・技能・知識が少なく、容易にできる。

direct：回り道・仲介・遠回しな表現を用いず、対象へ直接向かう。
candid：不都合なことも隠さず、率直かつ正直に話す。

en: straightforward describes a clear and uncomplicated procedure or meaning, or an honest and direct person or statement.
easy describes something requiring little effort, skill, or knowledge.
simple describes something with few elements or little conceptual complexity.
uncomplicated describes a situation, relationship, or system lacking difficult complexities.
clear describes meaning, explanation, or circumstances that are unambiguous and readily understood.
direct describes movement or communication that reaches its object without diversion, intermediaries, or indirect wording.
candid describes honest speech that does not conceal inconvenient facts or opinions.
blunt describes direct speech that may sound insensitive, abrupt, or insufficiently tactful.

etymology.ja: straightforward は straight と forward から成る。straight は中英語 streight に由来し、もとは stretch「伸ばす」と関係する古英語 streccan の過去分詞に基づき、「伸ばされた、まっすぐな」という意味を持った。forward は古英語 foreweard「前方へ」に由来する。両語を合わせた straightforward は、文字どおりには「まっすぐ前方へ向かう」を意味し、曲がり道や障害がないことから、「単純明快な」「率直な」という抽象的意味へ発達した。
etymology.en: Straightforward is formed from straight and forward. Straight developed through Middle English streight from a past-participial form related to Old English streccan, to stretch, and originally conveyed the idea of being stretched or extended in a direct line. Forward derives from Old English foreweard, meaning toward the front. Their combination literally meant proceeding directly ahead. From the absence of turns, diversions, or obstacles developed the figurative meanings uncomplicated, readily understood, direct, and honest.

note.en: Emphasizes the absence of complex elements, problems, or troublesome circumstances.

note.en: Describes facts, distinctions, or decisions that leave little room for doubt or ambiguity.

note.en: Describes speech or action that reaches its object without diversion or indirect language.

note.ja: 自分の考えや不都合な事実を隠さず、率直に述べる。
note.en: Describes openly and honestly expressing one's views or inconvenient facts.

usage.figurative: After be or remain, the phrase commonly means undecided, uncertain, or unsettled.
usage.literal: With verbs of throwing, rising, or remaining above the ground, it can refer literally to an airborne position.
usage.subject: Common figurative subjects include plans, dates, arrangements, decisions, negotiations, and outcomes.
usage.still: Still frequently emphasizes that a decision has not yet been reached despite the passage of time.
usage.leave: Leave something up in the air means to fail or decline to settle it.
usage.register: Informal to neutral and common in conversation, journalism, and workplace communication.
usage.contrast: Be in the air without up commonly means that something is widely felt, expected, or present, not that it is undecided.
usage.hyphenation: The idiomatic phrase is normally written without hyphens after a verb. Before a noun, writers generally prefer an alternative such as unresolved rather than an up-in-the-air decision.

ja: 物が地面から離れて空中にある
予定・計画・日程などがまだ決定されていない
問題・交渉・将来などが未解決で見通せない
外部事情の変化によって、以前の決定や計画が不確実になっている
複数の可能性が残り、最終的な結果が定まっていない
en: physically above the ground or moving through the air
not yet decided, especially of a plan, arrangement, or date
unresolved and uncertain, especially of an issue, negotiation, or future
made uncertain because external circumstances may alter an earlier plan or decision
having several possibilities still open and no settled outcome

nuance.ja: up in the air の比喩用法は、物が地上の安定した場所に着かず、空中に浮いたままであるというイメージに基づく。Our travel plans are still up in the air. は、単に細部を決めていないだけの場合もあれば、予算・許可・天候などの事情で旅行そのものが実現するか不明な場合もある。undecided が意思決定の未完了を客観的に述べるのに対し、up in the air は、状況全体の不安定さや先行きの見えなさを感じさせる。leave something up in the air は、結論を出さず宙ぶらりんにしておくことを表す。なお、Excitement is in the air. の be in the air は「雰囲気として漂っている」であり、up in the air とは意味が異なる。
nuance.en: The figurative use of up in the air is based on the image of an object that has not reached a stable position on the ground and remains suspended. Our travel plans are still up in the air may mean merely that details have not been fixed, or that the trip itself is uncertain because of budget, permission, weather, or another external factor. Undecided objectively describes the absence of a decision, whereas up in the air more vividly suggests instability and an inability to see how the situation will develop. Leave something up in the air means to leave it without a conclusion. Be in the air, as in Excitement is in the air, instead means that a feeling or expectation is widely present.

ja: up in the air：計画・日程・結果などが確定せず、不安定で先行きが見えない。
undecided：複数の選択肢からまだ決定がなされていない。
uncertain：結果・事実・将来などが確実ではないことを広く表す。
unresolved：問題・争点・対立などに解決や結論が出ていない。
in limbo：決定権や進展を失い、長期間宙ぶらりんの状態に置かれている。
hanging in the balance：二つの結果のどちらになるか分からず、重大な局面にある。
up for grabs：まだ誰のものとも決まっておらず、獲得・選択の機会が開かれている。
in the air：感情・変化・期待などが周囲に漂い、多くの人に感じられる。
en: up in the air describes a plan, date, or outcome that remains unsettled, unstable, and difficult to predict.
undecided means that no choice has yet been made among available alternatives.
uncertain is the broad term for an outcome, fact, or future that is not known with confidence.
unresolved describes a problem, issue, or dispute for which no solution or conclusion has been reached.
in limbo suggests being left without progress or a decision, often for a prolonged period.
hanging in the balance describes an important situation whose outcome could still go either way.
up for grabs means not yet possessed, awarded, or allocated and still available to be won.
in the air means that a feeling, change, or expectation is generally present or perceptible.

etymology.ja: air は古フランス語 air、ラテン語 āēr を経て、ギリシャ語 āḗr「空気・霧」に由来する。up in the air は文字どおり、物が地面や固定された場所を離れて空中にあることを表す。投げ上げられた物は、着地するまで位置や結果が定まらない。この物理的な不安定さから、19世紀頃までに、計画・問題・結論などが確定せず宙に浮いている状態を表す比喩として定着した。日本語の「宙に浮く」と非常によく似た概念形成である。
etymology.en: Air entered English through Old French air and Latin aer from Greek aer, meaning air, mist, or the lower atmosphere. Up in the air literally describes an object above the ground or away from a fixed position. Once an object has been thrown upward, its position and final destination remain unsettled until it lands. From this physical instability, the phrase became established by the nineteenth century as a metaphor for plans, questions, and outcomes that had not yet been settled. Its conceptual development closely resembles the Japanese metaphor of something floating in midair.

note.en: Describes being stuck in an indefinite state while awaiting a decision or progress.

note.en: Describes a plan, issue, or situation that is not fixed or stable and remains open to change.

usage.variant: Both as right as rain and the shortened right as rain are standard idiomatic forms.
usage.health: Most commonly describes a person who is completely healthy or has recovered from a minor illness, injury, or exhaustion.
usage.function: It can also describe a repaired object, restored system, or situation returned to satisfactory order.
usage.linking_verbs: Commonly follows be, feel, look, or seem.
usage.causative: Get or have something right as rain means to restore it to proper working condition.
usage.register: Informal, reassuring, and especially associated with British English; it may sound traditional or mildly old-fashioned.
usage.severity: Usually used for temporary or relatively manageable problems and may sound dismissive if applied to a serious illness or injury.
usage.comparison: Despite its form, it does not make a literal logical comparison with rainfall; the phrase is lexicalized.

身体や気分が完全に正常で良好な状態にある
故障した機械・システムなどが修理され、正常に機能している

相手はまもなく回復するだろうと安心させる
en: completely healthy again after an illness, exhaustion, or minor injury
feeling entirely normal and well
restored to proper working order, especially of a machine or system
returned to a satisfactory and orderly condition
used to reassure someone that recovery will occur soon

nuance.ja: as right as rain は、単に状態が改善したというより、元どおり正常で問題のない状態へ回復したことを、明るく親しみのある調子で表す。A good night’s sleep and you’ll be right as rain. は、「一晩よく眠れば、すっかり元気になりますよ」という安心させる言い方である。人の健康が中心だが、機械や計画にも比喩的に使える。right はここでは「道徳的に正しい」ではなく、「正常な、申し分のない」という古くからの意味である。軽快な表現なので、重大な病気や長期的な障害について安易に用いると、相手の苦痛を軽視しているように聞こえることがある。
nuance.en: As right as rain suggests more than partial improvement: it presents a person or thing as restored to a normal, satisfactory, trouble-free condition. A good night's sleep and you'll be right as rain is a cheerful and familiar reassurance that complete recovery is expected. Health is its central domain, but it may also be applied figuratively to a repaired machine, restored system, or corrected situation. Right here does not mean morally correct; it uses the older sense healthy, proper, or in good order. Because the expression is lighthearted, using it casually about a serious illness or lasting disability may appear to minimize the person's suffering.

ja: as right as rain：不調から回復し、すっかり元気または完全に正常な状態である。
fit as a fiddle：非常に健康で体力も十分である。回復後である必要はない。
back to normal：病気・混乱・故障などの後、通常の状態へ戻っている。
as good as new：修理・回復によって、ほとんど新品同様の状態になっている。
on the mend：病気・けが・問題などが回復途中にある。まだ完全な状態とは限らない。
feel better：以前より体調・気分が改善しているが、完全回復とは限らない。
in good shape：人の健康・体力、または物の状態が良好である。
up and about：病気やけがの後、起き上がって日常的に動けるまで回復している。
en: as right as rain means completely recovered and restored to a normal, satisfactory condition.
fit as a fiddle means extremely healthy and energetic without requiring a preceding illness.
back to normal means returned to the usual state after illness, disruption, or malfunction.
as good as new means restored by repair or recovery to an almost new condition.
on the mend means recovering from illness, injury, or difficulty but not necessarily fully restored.
feel better means improved in health or mood without implying complete recovery.
in good shape describes good health, fitness, or physical condition.
up and about means sufficiently recovered from illness or injury to leave bed and resume ordinary movement.

etymology.ja: right は古英語 riht「正しい、適切な、まっすぐな」に由来し、そこから「正常な、健康な、申し分のない」という意味も発達した。rain は古英語 regn に由来する。right as rain は19世紀後半から20世紀初頭に定着した表現で、right と rain の頭韻、および短くリズミカルな音の組合せが普及に寄与したと考えられる。かつて英語には right as a trivet や right as nails など、right as ... の多様な比較表現が存在した。なぜ雨が正常さの基準なのかを説明する説は複数あるが、確実な単一起源は判明しておらず、韻律的な言葉遊びの要素が強い。
etymology.en: Right derives from Old English riht, meaning correct, proper, or straight, and also developed the senses normal, healthy, and in good order. Rain derives from Old English regn. Right as rain became established in the late nineteenth or early twentieth century, probably aided by the alliteration and compact rhythm of right and rain. English formerly had numerous comparisons built on right as, including right as a trivet and right as nails. Various explanations have been proposed for rain as the standard of correctness, but no single literal origin is securely established, and verbal rhythm and alliteration probably played a major role.

note.en: A direct and neutral expression indicating complete recovery from illness, injury, or loss.

usage.person: With identifies the person whose opinion agrees with the subject's opinion.
usage.topic: On or about identifies the matter on which the parties agree.
usage.negative: The negative form not see eye to eye is especially common and describes a continuing difference of opinion.
usage.degree: The expression normally suggests substantial or complete agreement on the relevant point, not merely partial agreement.
usage.subject: The subject is often plural or coordinated: The two parties see eye to eye.
usage.literal_warning: The modern expression is idiomatic and does not normally describe two people physically looking into each other's eyes.
usage.register: Neutral and suitable for conversation, journalism, business, and semi-formal professional communication.

ja: 二人以上が同じ意見・見解を持つ
特定の問題について完全または大筋で合意する
物事の見方・価値観・方針が一致する
対立していた者同士が共通認識に達する
en: for two or more people to hold the same opinion or view
to agree completely or substantially on a particular issue
to share the same perspective, values, or policy
for previously opposed parties to reach a common understanding

nuance.ja: see eye to eye は、同じ事実を知っているだけでなく、その評価や取るべき方針について見方が一致していることを表す。We agree. よりも、当事者が同じ視点から問題を見ているという比喩性がある。否定形 We don’t see eye to eye on everything. は、関係そのものが悪いと断定せずに意見の相違を述べられるため、職場や交渉でも便利である。通常は特定の論点についての一致を表し、二人があらゆる事柄で同じ意見を持つことまでは意味しない。また、finally see eye to eye は、議論や交渉を経て認識が一致したことを示すが、法的な合意や契約が成立したことを必ずしも意味しない。
nuance.en: See eye to eye means more than possessing the same factual information: it indicates that the parties evaluate the matter similarly or favor the same course of action. Compared with We agree, it retains the metaphor of viewing an issue from the same perspective. The negative sentence We don't see eye to eye on everything is useful in workplaces and negotiations because it acknowledges disagreement without necessarily suggesting that the relationship itself is hostile. The expression usually concerns a particular issue and does not mean that the people share every opinion. Finally see eye to eye indicates that views have converged after discussion or negotiation, but it does not necessarily mean that a legally binding agreement has been concluded.

ja: see eye to eye：特定の問題について同じ見方を持ち、意見が一致する。
agree：意見・提案・条件などが一致することを表す最も一般的な語。
be on the same page：状況・目的・計画について共通理解を持っている。
share someone’s view：ある人と同じ意見・見解を持つことを直接的に表す。
reach an agreement：議論・交渉を経て、具体的な条件や方針について合意に達する。
find common ground：対立する当事者が、双方の一致できる点を見つける。
agree to disagree：意見の一致を諦め、相違を残したまま争いを終える。
not see eye to eye：特定の問題について意見・見方が合わない。
en: see eye to eye means to share the same view and agree on a particular matter.
agree is the most general verb for sharing an opinion or accepting a proposal or condition.
be on the same page means to share an understanding of the situation, objective, or plan.
share someone's view directly states that one holds the same opinion as another person.
reach an agreement means to settle specific terms or a course of action through discussion or negotiation.
find common ground means to identify a point on which opposing parties can agree.
agree to disagree means to stop arguing while allowing the difference of opinion to remain.
not see eye to eye means to hold different views on a particular issue.

etymology.ja: see eye to eye は『旧約聖書』イザヤ書52章8節の英訳で知られるようになった表現で、欽定訳聖書には見張り人たちが eye to eye に見るという形で現れる。当初は「直接、明瞭に見る」「同じものを共に見る」という意味合いを持っていた。その後、同じ高さ・視点から物を見るという比喩的な理解が強まり、19世紀頃までに「意見が一致する」という現代的な意味が定着した。eye は古英語 ēage、see は古英語 sēon に由来する。
etymology.en: See eye to eye became widely known through Isaiah 52:8 in English translations of the Bible, including the King James Version, where watchmen are described as seeing eye to eye. The earlier expression conveyed seeing directly, clearly, or together. It later came to be understood metaphorically as viewing something from the same level or perspective, and by the nineteenth century the modern sense agree in opinion had become established. Eye derives from Old English eage, and see from Old English seon.

note.ja: 意見・事実認識・条件などが一致することを表す、最も一般的で中立的な語。
note.en: The most general and neutral verb for sharing an opinion or accepting facts or terms.

usage.object: It may be replaced by the information, claim, report, prediction, or statement being treated skeptically.

usage.american_variant: A grain of salt is the usual American form.

usage.meaning: The expression advises caution rather than necessarily declaring the information false.
usage.register: Informal to neutral and common in conversation, journalism, reviews, and semi-formal analysis.
usage.article: The conventional forms use a pinch of salt or a grain of salt.

ipa.us: /ˌteɪk ɪt wɪð ə ˌpɪntʃ əv ˈsɔːlt/
ipa.uk: /ˌteɪk ɪt wɪð ə ˌpɪntʃ əv ˈsɒlt/

ja: 情報・発言を完全には信用せず、多少疑って受け止める
噂・予測・宣伝文句などを額面どおりに信じない
情報源の偏り・誇張・不正確さを考慮して解釈する
主張を直ちに否定せず、裏付けを確認するまで判断を保留する
en: to treat information or a statement with some skepticism rather than accepting it completely
not to take a rumor, prediction, or promotional claim at face value
to interpret information while allowing for bias, exaggeration, or inaccuracy in its source
to reserve judgment about a claim until supporting evidence has been checked

nuance.ja: take it with a pinch of salt は、「その話は嘘だ」と断定するのではなく、情報の正確性には疑問があるため、割り引いて受け止めるべきだと示す。たとえば、誇張することで知られる人の話、匿名の噂、企業の自己評価、将来予測などに自然に使える。with skepticism より会話的で、相手の発言を正面から否定せずに注意を促せる。a large pinch of salt とすれば、ほとんど信用していないことをユーモラスに強調する。なお、重要な法律・医療・安全上の情報については、この表現だけで済ませず、根拠や問題点を具体的に示すほうが適切である。
nuance.en: Take it with a pinch of salt does not categorically declare that the information is false. It advises discounting it because its accuracy may be affected by exaggeration, bias, uncertainty, or an unreliable source. It is natural for stories told by someone known to exaggerate, anonymous rumors, corporate self-assessments, and forecasts. The phrase is more conversational than with skepticism and can recommend caution without directly accusing the speaker of lying. A large pinch of salt humorously indicates that very little confidence should be placed in the information. In serious legal, medical, or safety contexts, it is better to identify the evidential problem specifically rather than relying on this idiom alone.

ja: take it with a pinch of salt：情報を完全には信用せず、誇張や誤りの可能性を考慮して受け止める。
take it with a grain of salt：同じ意味を持つ、主にアメリカ英語の形。
be skeptical of：主張・情報の真実性について疑いを持つ、より直接的で中立的な表現。
not take something at face value：表面上示された内容を、そのまま真実とは受け取らない。
doubt：何かが真実・正確であるとは思わない。pinch of salt より否定的になり得る。
reserve judgment：十分な情報が得られるまで、肯定・否定いずれの判断も下さない。
fact-check：証拠や信頼できる情報源を用いて、主張の正確性を検証する。
dismiss：主張を検討に値しないものとして退ける。慎重に扱うだけの pinch of salt より強い。
en: take it with a pinch of salt means to allow for possible exaggeration or error instead of fully believing information.
take it with a grain of salt is the chiefly American form with the same meaning.
be skeptical of directly and neutrally expresses doubt about the truth of a claim or information.
not take something at face value means not to accept its surface presentation as the complete truth.
doubt means to regard something as unlikely to be true or accurate and may express stronger disbelief.
reserve judgment means to reach neither a positive nor a negative conclusion until more information is available.
fact-check means to verify a claim against evidence and reliable sources.
dismiss means to reject a claim as unworthy of consideration and is stronger than merely treating it cautiously.

etymology.ja: この表現の遠い背景として、古代ローマの大プリニウスが記録した毒への処方に、ラテン語 addito salis grano「一粒の塩を加えて」に相当する文言があることがしばしば挙げられる。そこから cum grano salis「一粒の塩とともに」が、機知・慎重さ・留保をもって受け取るという意味で用いられるようになったとされる。ただし、古代の処方と現代のイディオムを直接結ぶ歴史的経路には不確かな点もある。英語では grain of salt が先に定着し、イギリス英語では20世紀に pinch of salt が一般的になった。pinch は親指と指先でつまめる少量を意味する。
etymology.en: The expression is often associated with a passage recorded by Pliny the Elder containing the Latin words corresponding to add a grain of salt as part of an antidote. The later Latin phrase cum grano salis came to suggest receiving something with wit, caution, or reservation. The precise historical path connecting the ancient prescription to the modern idiom is not entirely certain. Grain of salt became established in English, while the variant pinch of salt became especially common in twentieth-century British English. A pinch is the small amount that can be held between a thumb and fingertip.

note.ja: 情報の真実性・正確性を疑い、批判的に検討することを中立的に表す。
note.en: Neutrally describes doubting and critically examining the truth or accuracy of information.

note.ja: 言葉や外観から直接受ける印象を、そのまま完全な真実として受け入れない。
note.en: Means not accepting the immediate wording or appearance as the complete truth.

note.ja: 情報源の偏り・不確実性などを考慮し、主張の価値や信頼度を割り引く。
note.en: To reduce the weight or credibility given to a claim because of bias, uncertainty, or another weakness.

note.ja: 証拠が十分になるまで、主張が正しいかどうかの最終判断を保留する。
note.en: To postpone a final conclusion about a claim until sufficient evidence is available.

patterns: pull my / your / his / her / our / their leg
someone must be pulling my leg

usage.possessive: The possessive normally agrees with the person being teased: pull my leg, pull her leg, pull their legs.
usage.progressive: The progressive form is especially common when reacting to a joke in progress: Are you pulling my leg?
usage.plural: With several people, both pull their leg and pull their legs occur, though their legs is logically regular.
usage.literal: The same words can describe physically pulling a person's leg, but context normally makes the idiomatic meaning clear.
usage.intent: The idiom usually describes playful deception rather than a serious attempt to obtain money, advantage, or confidential information.
usage.response: I'm only pulling your leg reveals that the preceding statement was a joke.
usage.british_response: Pull the other one is a chiefly British humorous response meaning I do not believe you.
usage.register: Informal and most natural among friends, relatives, and familiar colleagues.

ja: 冗談の嘘を本当らしく言って人をからかう
人を一時的に信じ込ませ、その反応を面白がる
深刻そうな話が実は冗談であると後から明かす
文字どおり、人の脚を引っ張る
en: to tease someone by telling them something untrue as though it were serious
to make someone temporarily believe a joke in order to enjoy their reaction
to reveal afterward that an apparently serious statement was not true
literally, to pull a person's leg physically

nuance.ja: pull someone’s leg の中心は、相手を傷つけたり利益を得たりすることではなく、本当らしい冗談によって軽く欺き、その反応を楽しむことである。I won the lottery. — Are you pulling my leg? なら、「宝くじに当たったなんて冗談ではないか」と疑っている。tease は言葉・行動を問わず人をからかう広い語だが、pull someone’s leg は、虚偽の情報を一時的に信じさせるという仕掛けを含みやすい。ただし、相手にとって敏感な話題を使った場合、話者に冗談のつもりがあっても不快な欺瞞になり得る。正式な職場や依頼人とのやり取りでは、冗談だと分かる関係と状況でのみ使うのが安全である。
nuance.en: The central idea of pull someone’s leg is not harming the person or obtaining an advantage but briefly misleading them with a plausible joke and enjoying their reaction. In I won the lottery. — Are you pulling my leg?, the listener suspects that the supposedly serious news is invented. Tease is a broad verb covering many kinds of playful words and behavior, whereas pull someone’s leg often involves getting the person to believe false information temporarily. A joke involving a sensitive subject may still become hurtful deception even if the speaker intended playfulness. In formal workplaces or communication with clients, the expression and the behavior it describes are safest only where the relationship and context make the joke unmistakable.

ja: pull someone’s leg：本当らしい冗談を信じ込ませて、軽く人をからかう。
tease：言葉・行動・特徴などについて人をからかうことを広く表す。
kid：冗談を言う・からかうという口語的な動詞。I’m kidding. が非常に一般的。
joke：笑わせる目的で冗談を言う。必ずしも相手を一時的に欺かない。
play a prank on：仕掛けや行動を用いた、より具体的ないたずらを人にする。
wind someone up：主にイギリス英語で、冗談や挑発によって人を信じ込ませたり苛立たせたりする。
deceive：真実を隠して人に誤ったことを信じさせる。冗談とは限らず、より重大である。
make fun of：人の特徴・失敗などを笑いものにするため、傷つける可能性が高い。
en: pull someone’s leg means to tease someone by getting them to believe a plausible joke temporarily.
tease broadly describes playful or unkind remarks and behavior directed at another person.
kid is an informal verb meaning to joke or tease, especially common in I'm kidding.
joke means to say something for amusement without necessarily misleading a particular person.
play a prank on means to perform a more concrete practical joke involving an arranged trick or action.
wind someone up is a chiefly British expression for teasing, misleading, or deliberately irritating someone.
deceive means to cause someone to believe something false and may involve serious or malicious dishonesty.
make fun of means to ridicule a person's characteristics or mistakes and is more likely to cause hurt.

etymology.ja: pull someone’s leg は19世紀後半の英語で「人をからかう・欺く」という意味で現れた。脚を引っかけて転倒させるいたずらに由来するという説や、路上の窃盗犯が被害者を倒す行為に由来するという説がしばしば紹介されるが、それらを裏付ける確実な証拠は乏しい。したがって、正確な起源は不明とするのが安全である。物理的に脚を引いて相手の安定を崩すというイメージが、心理的に相手を惑わせる軽い欺きへ転じた可能性はある。
etymology.en: Pull someone’s leg appeared in late nineteenth-century English with the meaning tease or deceive. It is often claimed to derive either from tripping someone as a practical joke or from street thieves pulling victims to the ground. These stories lack firm historical evidence, so the expression's precise origin remains uncertain. The physical image of pulling a person's leg and disturbing their balance may nevertheless have encouraged the figurative idea of momentarily unsettling or misleading someone.

note.ja: 冗談を言って人をからかう口語的な動詞。pull someone’s leg より簡潔で幅広い。
note.en: An informal verb meaning to joke with or tease someone, broader and more concise than pull someone’s leg.

note.ja: 人を遊び半分でからかう場合と、繰り返し傷つける場合の両方に使える一般語。
note.en: A general verb covering both affectionate playfulness and repeated hurtful provocation.

note.ja: 冗談を信じ込ませたり、わざと苛立たせたりする主にイギリス英語の表現。
note.en: A chiefly British expression meaning to mislead someone jokingly or deliberately make them annoyed.

note.ja: 人を驚かせたり騙したりする冗談・いたずらを仕掛ける。
note.en: To direct a joke or trick at someone in order to surprise or mislead them.

ja: I’ve been chosen to fly to the Moon next week. — Are you pulling my leg? — 「来週、月へ行く人に選ばれたんだ」「からかっているんでしょう？」

You expect me to believe that the meeting ended early? You must be pulling my leg. — 会議が早く終わったなんて、私が信じると思いますか。冗談でしょう。

Don’t worry—the restaurant isn’t really closed. I was only pulling your leg.
For a moment, she believed his story, but then she realized he was pulling her leg.

patterns: spill the beans about something to someone

usage.fixed_object: The idiom normally uses the beans as a fixed object; replacing beans with another noun removes the idiomatic meaning.
usage.about_or_on: About or on introduces the secret subject: spill the beans about the surprise party.
usage.to_person: To identifies the recipient of the information: spill the beans to a reporter.
usage.intention: The disclosure may be deliberate, reluctant, or accidental.
usage.imperative: Spill the beans! is a playful or insistent request for someone to reveal the full story.
usage.passive: The beans have been spilled means that the secret is now known, although the passive is less common than the active.
usage.register: Informal and conversational; disclose or reveal is more appropriate in formal legal and business writing.
usage.past_form: Spilled is standard throughout the English-speaking world; spilt also occurs, particularly in British English.

ja: 秘密・内密の計画などを明かす
隠されていた事情や詳しい話をすべて打ち明ける
秘密をうっかり漏らしてしまう
質問・説得・圧力などを受けて、知っている情報を話す
相手に秘密や詳しい事情を話すよう促す
en: to reveal a secret or confidential plan
to disclose the full details of a previously hidden situation
to let secret information become known accidentally
to reveal what one knows after questioning, persuasion, or pressure
used imperatively to urge someone to tell the full story

nuance.ja: spill the beans は、情報を事務的に伝えるのではなく、それまで隠されていた事柄が外へ出てしまうという、くだけた比喩である。誰かが誕生日会の計画をうっかり話した場合にも、秘密を問い詰められてついに明かした場合にも使える。Spill the beans! は親しい相手に「もったいぶらず教えて」と促す軽快な表現だが、相手に守秘義務がある場面では不適切になり得る。reveal は意図的か偶発的かを限定しない中立語であるのに対し、spill には、容器から中身がこぼれるように、情報の管理が失われたという感触がある。ただし、このイディオム自体は通常、国家機密などの極めて深刻な漏洩より、日常的な秘密や意外な情報に使われる。
nuance.en: Spill the beans does not describe the neutral transmission of information. It informally depicts something previously contained or hidden escaping into the open. It can describe accidentally mentioning a surprise party or finally revealing a secret after persistent questioning. Spill the beans! is a lively way of saying Stop keeping us in suspense and tell us, but it may be inappropriate where the listener has a duty of confidentiality. Reveal is neutral as to intention, whereas spill suggests that control over the information has been lost, like the contents of a container being scattered. The idiom is normally used for personal secrets, gossip, and surprising information rather than the most serious forms of classified disclosure.

ja: spill the beans：それまで隠されていた秘密・計画・詳しい事情を明かす。
reveal：未知・秘密だった事実を明らかにする中立的な語。
disclose：情報、特に秘密・利害関係・法的事項などを正式に開示する。
let the cat out of the bag：秘密を、特にうっかり漏らしてしまう。
give the game away：言動によって秘密の計画・正体・真意を露見させる。
spill one’s guts：個人的な悩み・秘密・感情を洗いざらい話す。より生々しくくだけた表現。
come clean：隠していた真実、特に自分の不正・責任について正直に告白する。
leak：秘密情報を、しばしば権限なく報道機関などへ意図的に流す。
en: spill the beans means to reveal a secret, plan, or full hidden story.
reveal is the neutral verb for making a previously unknown or hidden fact known.
disclose means to make information formally known, especially confidential, financial, or legal information.
let the cat out of the bag means to reveal a secret, particularly by accident.
give the game away means to expose a secret plan, identity, or intention through one's behavior or words.
spill one’s guts means to reveal deeply personal secrets, worries, or feelings in a vivid informal manner.
come clean means to admit the truth honestly, especially about one's own wrongdoing or responsibility.
leak means to provide confidential information without authorization, often deliberately to the media.

etymology.ja: spill は古英語 spillan「殺す、破壊する、無駄にする」などに由来し、中英語以降、液体や物を容器からこぼす意味を発達させた。spill the beans は20世紀初頭のアメリカ英語で、秘密を漏らす意味に定着した。古代ギリシャで白黒の豆を用いて投票し、壺を倒すと結果が明らかになったことに由来するという説がよく紹介されるが、それを現代の英語表現へ直接結び付ける確実な証拠はない。正確な起源は不明であり、容器の中に隠れていた豆がこぼれて見えるという分かりやすい比喩が意味の定着を助けたと考えられる。
etymology.en: Spill derives from Old English spillan, with meanings including kill, destroy, or waste, and later developed the familiar sense of causing liquid or objects to fall from a container. Spill the beans became established in early twentieth-century American English with the meaning reveal a secret. A popular explanation connects it with supposed ancient Greek voting practices in which colored beans were kept in a container and spilling them exposed the result. Firm evidence directly linking that practice to the modern English idiom is lacking, however, and its precise origin remains uncertain. The transparent image of previously hidden contents becoming visible probably aided its development.

synonyms.word: let the cat out of the bag

note.en: Often describes revealing a secret unintentionally, especially one involving a planned surprise.

note.ja: 隠されていた事実・正体・情報を明らかにする、広く中立的な動詞。

note.ja: 自分が隠していた不正・責任・真実を、最終的に正直に認める。
note.en: To finally admit a truth one has concealed, especially concerning one's own misconduct or responsibility.

note.ja: 内心の感情や個人的な秘密を、包み隠さず大量に話す非常にくだけた表現。
note.en: A highly informal expression for disclosing personal feelings or secrets fully and emotionally.

patterns: Boy, can you say that again!

usage.function: Used as a response expressing strong agreement with the immediately preceding statement.
usage.not_literal: In ordinary idiomatic use, it does not actually request repetition.
usage.that: That refers to the proposition or opinion expressed by the previous speaker.
usage.can: Can conveys that the statement is so true that it deserves to be repeated.
usage.register: Informal and conversational; suitable among friends and familiar colleagues.
usage.tone: It often responds to complaints or emphatic evaluations, but it can also agree with positive statements.
usage.intonation: Falling or emphatic intonation signals agreement. Confused or questioning intonation may cause it to be interpreted literally.
usage.variation: The marked form Can you say that again! can express especially emphatic agreement, but the standard formula begins with You.

ja: 相手の発言に全面的・強く同意する
相手が述べたことは繰り返す価値があるほど正しいと認める
不満・疲労・困難などについて、自分も同じように強く感じていると示す
肯定的な評価や称賛について、まさにそのとおりだと応じる
en: to express complete or emphatic agreement with another person's statement
to indicate that a statement is so true that it deserves to be repeated
to show that one strongly shares another person's complaint, fatigue, or sense of difficulty
to agree enthusiastically with a positive evaluation or compliment

nuance.ja: You can say that again. は、相手の発言を単に正しいと認めるだけでなく、話者自身もその内容を強く実感していることを示す。This has been a long day. — You can say that again. なら、「本当に長い一日だった」という共通の疲労感を表す。文字どおりに解釈すれば相手へ繰り返しを許可する文だが、通常の会話では反復を求めていない。聞き取れずに繰り返してほしい場合は Could you say that again? と疑問文で尋ねる必要がある。強い同意としては温かく勢いがある一方、正式な会議や書面では Indeed.、I completely agree. などのほうが適切である。
nuance.en: You can say that again does more than acknowledge that the other person's statement is correct. It indicates that the speaker strongly shares the experience or evaluation. In This has been a long day. — You can say that again, both speakers feel the day's length and exhaustion. Literally, the sentence appears to permit repetition, but its normal conversational function is not to request it. If the speaker failed to hear and wants the words repeated, the appropriate question is Could you say that again? The idiom conveys warmth and energy, but Indeed or I completely agree is generally more suitable in a formal meeting or written document.

ja: you can say that again：相手の発言に、自分も強くそう思うと全面的に同意する。

I couldn’t agree more：これ以上同意できないほど全面的に賛成する。やや改まった場面にも使える。
absolutely：相手の発言・提案に強く同意する簡潔な応答。
that’s for sure：その点に疑いはないと、くだけた調子で同意する。
you said it：相手が自分の気持ちを的確に言い表したと認める。
tell me about it：自分も同じ不快な経験をよく知っていると共感する。主に否定的話題で使う。
hear, hear：公の場で発言への賛同を声に出して示す、伝統的な表現。
en: you can say that again expresses strong agreement and indicates that the speaker feels exactly the same way.
Could you say that again? genuinely asks for repetition because the listener did not hear or understand.
I couldn’t agree more expresses the highest degree of agreement and can suit somewhat more formal contexts.
absolutely is a concise response expressing strong agreement with a statement or proposal.
that’s for sure informally agrees that there can be no doubt about a particular point.
you said it acknowledges that the other person has expressed the speaker's own view exactly.
tell me about it indicates shared familiarity with an unpleasant experience and is used mainly with negative topics.
hear, hear is a traditional public expression of approval for a speaker's statement.

etymology.ja: この表現は、相手の発言が非常に正確であるため、「もう一度言ってもよいほどだ」と評価する誇張的な言い回しから成立した。say は古英語 secgan「言う」、again は古英語 onġēan「反対に、戻って」に由来し、のちに「もう一度」の意味を発達させた。20世紀前半までにアメリカ英語の口語的な同意表現として定着し、その後広く使われるようになった。現在では各語の文字どおりの意味より、強い賛同を示す一まとまりの談話表現として理解される。
etymology.en: The expression arose as a hyperbolic way of saying that another person's statement is so accurate that it could appropriately be repeated. Say derives from Old English secgan, while again developed from Old English ongean, originally meaning against or back and later once more. By the first half of the twentieth century, the full expression had become established as an informal formula of emphatic agreement in American English and subsequently spread more widely. Modern speakers normally process it as a single discourse formula rather than as literal permission to repeat the words.

note.ja: 完全な賛同を明示し、口語からやや改まった場面まで使える。
note.en: Explicitly expresses complete agreement and works from conversation to somewhat formal contexts.

note.ja: 相手が自分の考え・感情をまさに言い当てたと認める口語表現。
note.en: An informal response acknowledging that the other person has expressed one's own thought or feeling exactly.

note.ja: 相手の発言の真実性には疑いがないと、気軽に強調する。
note.en: A casual response emphasizing that there is no doubt about the truth of the statement.

note.ja: 自分も同じ不満・苦労を十分経験していると示す。文字どおり説明を求める意味ではない。
note.en: Indicates extensive personal experience of the same difficulty and does not literally request an explanation.

usage.article: The fixed expression normally uses the definite article: the bandwagon.
usage.variant: Get on, climb on, and join the bandwagon have similar meanings; jump on emphasizes quick or eager participation.
usage.evaluation: The expression is often critical, implying imitation, conformity, or opportunism after success has become visible.
usage.neutral_use: It can also be used humorously or neutrally when someone finally adopts a popular product or activity.
usage.subject: The subject may be a person, company, political group, media organization, or entire industry.
usage.register: Informal to neutral and common in journalism, political commentary, business, and conversation.
usage.opposite: Resist the bandwagon or go against the trend expresses refusal to follow popular opinion.

ja: 人気が高まっている流行・活動・考え方に加わる
成功が見えてから、利益や支持を得るために便乗する
多数派の意見・政治運動などへ追随する
競合他社の成功を見て、同種の商品・技術・戦略を採用する
話題の製品・趣味などを遅れて試し始める
en: to join a trend, activity, or idea that is becoming popular
to associate oneself with apparent success in order to gain advantage or approval
to follow a majority opinion or political movement
to adopt a product, technology, or strategy after seeing competitors succeed with it
to begin using a fashionable product or pursuing a popular hobby after others

nuance.ja: jump on the bandwagon は、話者がその対象の本質的価値よりも、すでに生じている人気・勢い・成功に引かれて参加したと見る表現である。そのため Companies are jumping on the AI bandwagon. は、企業がAIを十分に理解して導入しているというより、流行に乗り遅れまいとして次々にAIを掲げているという批判を含み得る。jump は、急いで機会へ飛び乗る印象を強める。もっとも、I finally jumped on the bandwagon and bought one. のように、自分が人気商品を試したことを軽く自嘲する場合には、強い非難はない。単に早期に新技術を採用することを肯定的に述べたい場合は adopt、embrace、get on board with などがより中立的である。
nuance.en: Jump on the bandwagon suggests that participation is motivated by existing popularity, momentum, or visible success rather than solely by the intrinsic merit of the idea. Companies are jumping on the AI bandwagon may criticize businesses for displaying enthusiasm for AI merely to avoid appearing outdated, without understanding how to use it. Jump strengthens the impression of hurriedly seizing an opportunity. The phrase is not always strongly critical, however. In I finally jumped on the bandwagon and bought one, it can humorously acknowledge one's own delayed adoption of a popular product. To describe adoption positively and neutrally, verbs such as adopt, embrace, or get on board with may be preferable.

ja: jump on the bandwagon：人気や成功が見えてから、流行・運動・戦略などに便乗して加わる。
follow a trend：社会・市場などの一般的な傾向に従う。日和見的という非難は必須ではない。
get on board：計画・考え方を理解して支持・参加する。協力的で肯定的な響きを持ちやすい。
join the crowd：多くの人がしていることに自分も加わる、口語的な表現。
go with the flow：周囲の状況や他者の選択に逆らわず、自然な流れに従う。
follow suit：他者の行動を見て、同じ行動を取る。
cash in on：流行・評判・機会を利用して金銭的利益を得る。便乗の利益面を強調する。
be an early adopter：製品・技術が一般化する前の早い段階で採用する。bandwagon の後発性と対照的。
en: jump on the bandwagon means to join a trend, movement, or strategy after its popularity or success has become visible.
follow a trend means to act in accordance with a general social or market tendency without necessarily implying opportunism.
get on board means to understand, support, and participate in a plan or idea and often sounds cooperative and positive.
join the crowd informally means to begin doing what many other people are already doing.
go with the flow means to adapt to circumstances and follow others without resistance.
follow suit means to perform the same action after observing another person or organization.
cash in on means to exploit a trend, reputation, or opportunity for financial gain.
be an early adopter means to use a product or technology before it becomes mainstream, contrasting with the bandwagon's late participation.

etymology.ja: bandwagon は band「楽団」と wagon「荷馬車」を組み合わせた19世紀のアメリカ英語で、もとはサーカスの行列で楽団を乗せる華やかな馬車を指した。政治運動が群衆を集めるためにこのような馬車を利用するようになると、人気候補の側へ移って支持を表明することが get on the bandwagon と呼ばれるようになった。そこから政治以外にも広がり、勢いのある流行・考え・事業などへ、成功が見えてから参加することを意味するようになった。jump は、動いている馬車へ機会を逃さず飛び乗るような、急な便乗のイメージを加える。
etymology.en: Bandwagon is a nineteenth-century American compound of band and wagon. It originally denoted the conspicuous wagon carrying a musical band in a circus parade. Political campaigns used such wagons to attract crowds, and joining the side of a popular candidate came to be described as getting on the bandwagon. The image spread beyond politics to participation in any trend, idea, or venture whose momentum and success were already apparent. Jump adds the vivid suggestion of hurriedly leaping onto a wagon that is already moving so as not to miss the opportunity.

note.ja: 自分で判断するより、多数の人と同じ考え・行動を選ぶことに焦点を置く。
note.en: Emphasizes choosing the same opinion or behavior as the majority rather than deciding independently.

note.ja: 先に行動した人・組織を見て、それと同じ行動を取る。
note.en: To take the same action after observing what another person or organization has done.

note.ja: 人気・出来事・評判などを利用し、利益を得ようとする。より露骨に利得を強調する。
note.en: To exploit popularity, an event, or a reputation for gain, with a more explicit emphasis on profit.

note.ja: 計画・運動・考え方を支持し、協力者として加わる。通常は bandwagon より肯定的。
note.en: To support and participate in a plan, movement, or idea, normally with a more positive tone than bandwagon.

I resisted buying one for years, but I finally jumped on the bandwagon. — 私は何年も買わずにいたが、ついに流行に乗って一つ購入した。
